example.title: Patch Street Bridge, Patch Street over Kohanza Brook

brief: Single segmental stone arch of 32 ft span built by a local stonemason for the city after an 1869 flood: split-granite rubble spandrels and approach walls, a ring of long thin dressed voussoirs, and a low rubble parapet that is only a course or two above the roadway. The street runs flat over it with a sidewalk on each side behind chain-link fences, with drains and a brick sewer let through the arch. Set in a working-class residential neighbourhood of frame houses, in a shallow stony brook between rubble-walled banks.
